clue.text: Top desire is to see son promoted

indicators.note: promoted means moved up the order, so the son's letter is shifted nearer the front of the word for desire

parts.note: desire, as in a thirst for knowledge, is a craving
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent's dearest wish is to watch their boy get a promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' lifts the S of THIRST up from fifth place to second, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved cotton garment is a top, the general word for upper-body clothing.

clue.text: Information about male agents

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for information goes round the male's letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'

explanation.surface: A report giving details on men who work as agents.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Government men were the FBI's special agents in American slang of the 1930s.

clue.text: One leader of Christians following line in Church, right?

definitions.text: One leader of Christians following line in Church, right?

indicators.note: following means the one and the Christians' leader come after the church-and-right group
in means the line's letter goes inside the letters for Church

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from Christians

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is proper that one who guides Christians toes the line of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: a clergyman leads Christians and follows Church teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman or priest is a leader of a Christian congregation who keeps to the Church's line.

clue.text: Embattled mission cut short in town leading to tragedy

indicators.note: in means the shortened mission goes inside the word for town

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the mission's name is removed

parts.note: the Alamo was the Texan mission besieged by Mexican forces in 1836

explanation.surface: A besieged outpost in a town is the start of a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embattled' is a pointer to the famous 1836 siege in Texas; 'cut short' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster or catastrophe, a synonym of tragedy in its everyday sense.

clue.text: Some obstacles to leniency, like articles for fencing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sentencing note: certain factors stand in the way of leniency for the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: Fencing here is not swordplay or garden fences but receiving stolen goods: a fence is a dealer in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence handles pilfered goods, so items suited to fencing are ones that were taken by theft.

clue.text: For a nut, flying must involve British aero-engine

indicators.note: involve means take in, so the shuffled letters close round the British letter
flying means the letters are sent all over the place and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: For a fanatic, flying has to include a British jet engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a nut' reads as 'for an enthusiast', but it is the fodder for 'flying'; 'must involve' then takes in the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of jet engine with a large front fan, used on most airliners, so an aircraft power unit.

clue.text: Grass repeatedly folded over

parts.note: bent is a kind of coarse grass
double, as in saying something double, means twice over

explanation.surface: A lawn's grass flattened again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: BENT is a genus of grass, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stooped at the waist, as in doubled up with pain or laughter, is being folded over.

clue.text: A woman claiming conjugal rights in classic novel

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the woman's word holds the bed inside it

parts.note: a dame is a woman, in old-fashioned or American slang
bed stands for the marital rights of sharing a bed

explanation.surface: A wife demanding her marital rights in a famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjugal rights' is a euphemism standing for the marriage bed; 'claiming' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1859 debut work of fiction, a Victorian classic named after its carpenter hero.

clue.text: Music last to be disseminated in shared programming

indicators.note: disseminated means spread around, so these letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The music comes last when it is time to broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be disseminated' signals rearranging MUSICLAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast transmitted at once on radio and television, or several channels, is programming that is shared.

clue.text: Recalled bar closing early to finish bit of plumbing

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the shortened word is read backwards
closing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: bar in the sense of except, as is but in 'all but one'
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A pub, called back to close early, finishing a plumbing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means BUT; 'closing early' drops its T, and 'Recalled' turns BU into UB.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved section of waste pipe under a sink, holding water to block drain smells, is a plumbing part.

clue.text: Champion losing first place — just outside the bull

indicators.note: losing first place means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: A champion who lost the title finishes just behind the bullish leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first place' looks like sporting rank but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard or archery target, the ring immediately surrounding the bullseye is the inner.

clue.text: I'd album redone to contain it, having not planned ahead

indicators.note: contain means hold inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the word it
redone means made again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer remakes their record with the old track included, all without a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redone' scrambles the first two words and 'to contain' wraps the result round 'it'; the split of the anagram is decided by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means at one's pleasure, so done on the spur of the moment, improvised.

clue.text: Just gutted, backing party dumping leader — choice of direction here

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the two letters are swapped round
gutted means the insides are removed, keeping only the outside letters of Just
dumping its leader means the party word loses its first letter

parts.note: a function is a party or formal gathering

explanation.surface: Merely gutted after backing a party that dropped its leader, a voter must now choose a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves JT from Just; 'backing' turns it to TJ. 'dumping leader' takes F from FUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A road meeting where one route ends at another, forcing a turn left or right, offers a choice of way.

clue.text: Urinal echo reverberating, not exactly impressive

indicators.note: reverberating means bouncing around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The echo in a gents' toilet booming round is hardly grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverberating' signals rearranging URINALECHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking in bravery or grandeur means falling short of being impressive or heroic in scale.

clue.text: Hurried with cut, capturing traces of human origin in feature of violin …

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the cut word closes round the two traced letters
with a cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fled means hurried away

indicators.note: traces are faint signs, here the first letters of human and origin

explanation.surface: A rushed incision reveals human evidence on a violin...
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which keeps the violin theme; 'with cut', 'traces of' and 'capturing' are the three indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins have two sound openings shaped like an italic letter cut into the belly beside the bridge.

clue.text: … or different approach to strings (my other playing)

indicators.note: playing means performing freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the violin scene: a new way to treat the strings, playing my second instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings' links to the violin of the previous clue but means the particles of string theory.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this unifies the rival versions of string theory, an alternative framework for strings.

clue.text: Chooses wrong people to show fashion in female surroundings

indicators.note: in means the fashioning word goes within the female's letters
surroundings means the female word forms the outer frame

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl or unmarried woman
to cast is to fashion or shape, as metal in a mould

explanation.surface: A director picks the wrong models for a fashion show amid women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a link here, not a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: A director who gives roles to unsuitable actors picks the wrong performers for the parts.

clue.text: Expression of feeling but misplaced in our street

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word our

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong spot, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An emotional rant is out of place on our road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' scrambles 'but', and 'in' sets it among the letters of 'our' before the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fit of anger or tears is a release of emotion, an uncontrolled display.

clue.text: Elevate no prow of boat in middle of Henley

indicators.note: in means the no-and-prow letters sit inside the middle of Henley
the middle of Henley is all of it but the ends

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of boat

explanation.surface: No rowing boat's prow is raised at Henley.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous rowing regatta, which shapes the surface; 'middle of', 'prow of' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage, or to dignify them, is to elevate them.

clue.text: Caught English men drifting to garden workshop?

indicators.note: to means added onto what comes before
drifting means wandering out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
a shed is a hut in a garden, often used as a workshop

explanation.surface: Englishmen wander off to potter in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' turns MEN into NME.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled in a net is entangled, trapped, as in caught up in a web of lies.

clue.text: Minor argument about river fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quarrel word goes round the river letter

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A little quarrel over a fish caught in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SPAT round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-family species of the sea, eaten whole or tinned, is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Mark in hairstyle's a dreadful spot, a real shock

indicators.note: in means the mark's letter goes inside the hairstyle's letters

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut, and the 's gives BOBS
M stands for the German mark, the old currency
hell is a dreadful place

explanation.surface: Finding a blemish in one's haircut is a dreadful, shocking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro, so Mark capitalised gives M; 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden, devastating piece of news is a great surprise, a metaphor from an explosive shell.

clue.text: Second feature showing millions invested in US guy before contest

indicators.note: before means this group comes ahead of the contest word
invested in means put inside, so the millions' letter goes within the US guy

parts.note: bo is US slang for a pal or buddy
to vie is to compete or contest

explanation.surface: A film shown after spending millions on an American star ahead of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A second feature was the cheaper film in a cinema double bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-budget pictures were shown as the lesser half of a double bill, the support to the main film.

clue.text: Mistake tucking into short alcoholic drink

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the mistake word goes within the short word

parts.note: shy means short of, as in two shy of a full set
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A blunder made while downing a quick tot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a measure of spirits but means SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain is a type of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Mark of trainee: tardy after endless work piled up

indicators.note: after means the tardy word comes after the reversed letters
piled up means stacked upwards, so in this down clue the letters read from the bottom
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
late means tardy

explanation.surface: A trainee's mark is late because unfinished work piled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes Y off PLY, and 'piled up' reverses PL to LP.
explanation.definitionFit: British learner drivers must display a red letter sign on their car, the badge of a trainee.

clue.text: A burst of loud music, not initially very sharp

indicators.note: a burst means things blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A blast of loud music that was not so jarring to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very sharp' at the end looks like part of the music picture, but it is the definition; 'not initially' and 'burst of' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid in taste or tone, as in a biting remark, is extremely tart or cutting.

clue.text: I engaged in poor-quality, regressive communication

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the whole is read in reverse
engaged in means locked inside, so I goes within the word for poor-quality

parts.note: lame means feeble or poor-quality, as in a lame excuse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they took part in a shoddy, backward exchange of messages.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LAME making LIAME, and 'regressive' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message is a form of written correspondence.

clue.text: Top primate seen with cross

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: The leading ape looks angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or summit of something is its top.

clue.text: Skiers' aids, the foremost amongst the best Alpine resort services

indicators.note: the foremost of each word is its first letter, taken from the five words after

explanation.surface: Ski lifts are the top features among the finest Alpine resort facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Initial letters of 'the best Alpine resort services'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag lifts with a crossbar shaped like the letter pull skiers up the slope.

clue.text: I'm almost home — seriously

parts.note: I'm stands for I am: the I gives the letter, the contracted verb just joins the pieces
near means almost, as in a near miss
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A traveller announcing with feeling that they are nearly back home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read I'm as 'I [am] near nest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with sincerity and determination is doing it seriously.
